text:
nina: quick follow-up on the "affinity decoupling" spike — proposing a small-scope pattern: split request path into "map+fetch" (affinity map lookup + prefix fetch) and a pure executor. aim: reduce hotpath writes on the executor.

sam: short sketch of rollout?

nina: Phase 0: no-op router flag and shadowing. Phase 1: map+fetch returns read-only data (observe). Phase 2: enable read-through for an opt-in tenant set. Phase 3: full flip for matured tenants.

priya: latency concerns: extra RPCs can add tail. can we cache last-mapping on router for 100-200ms?

nina: yes — router-level LRU with small TTL. prefer colocated map service on same host in steady-state to avoid cross-node RPCs.

allan: what about batching semantics? executors should keep responsibility for batching. map+fetch should return hints (batch_key) but not perform coalescing.

priya: observability list: map-hit ratio, prefix-fetch latency, executor batch size distribution, per-tenant output-diff. tag spans with "affinity_phase" and "map_version".

sam: safety gates: start canary at 0.5% during high QPS, 3% low QPS. auto-rollback if p95 > baseline + 18% or error rate up 0.1% abs.

nina: migration note: backfill top-k prefixes per tenant via snapshot job. small correctness harness: replay 10k sessions and diff outputs.

deploy-bot: infra: feature-flag "affinity_decouple_observe" created. CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood.example/aff-decouple/1456

allan: cost model action: estimate extra RPCs per 1k requests and sidecar CPU. roll out to a subset of low-cost tenants first.

priya: test harness idea: golden-run with noise injection + hallucination-prone prompts. threshold: label drift <0.25% and BLEU-like score delta <1.5.

nina: I'll write a short RFC follow-up with timeline: 2w spike, 3w infra prep, 4-6w staged rollout. tagging @sam @priya @allan for review. :rocket:
